        On May 18, 2026, Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Ser-
vices Corporation (together, “Applicants”) filed their Objections to, and Motion to Strike, Interve-
nor Testimony (“Objections”). 1 There, the Applicants object to two direct-testimony attachments
of M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners’ witness Bob Davee on the grounds that those
attachments (Attachments RD-17 and RD-19) are “Hearsay; Non-Expert Opinion.” 2
        The M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners timely 3 respond to the Applicants’ Ob-
jections and respectfully request that the Administrative Law Judges (“ALJs”) (1) overrule the
Applicants’ objections to Attachments RD-17 and RD-19 and (2) deny the Applicants’ motion to
strike those two attachments.
         For reference, Attachment RD-17 is an excerpt from Texas Parks and Wildlife Depart-
ment’s (“TPWD’s”) 1974 report describing Texas’s major waterways and titled An Analysis of
Texas Waterways: A Report on the Physical Characteristics of Rivers, Streams, and Bayous in

 Texas (“TPWD Report”). 4 And Attachment RD-19 is a published study by Kiara C. Cushway and
Astrid N. Schwalb titled When rivers run dry: Perennial pools as ecological refuges for freshwater
mussels during drought (“Cushway Study”). 5
        As the M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners discuss below, Attachment RD-17 is
subject to two exceptions to the rule against hearsay. Attachment RD-19 is not hearsay. And neither
Attachment RD-17 nor Attachment RD-19 constitutes impermissible expert testimony by an un-
qualified witness because Mr. Davee is not providing any expert opinions concerning any technical
matters contained in those attachments.

                                                 I.       Hearsay
        Contrary to the Applicants’ generalized hearsay objection, 6 Attachments RD-17 and RD-
19 are not hearsay. Attachment RD-17 is subject to the public-records hearsay exception 7 and the
statements-in-ancient-documents hearsay exception. 8 And Attachment RD-19 is not hearsay be-
cause Mr. Davee did not include Attachment RD-19 in his testimony to prove the truth of the matter
asserted in the Cushway Study.

A.      Attachment RD-17 is subject to the public-records hearsay exception and the state-
        ments-in-ancient-documents hearsay exception.
        As the Applicants correctly state, “[h]earsay is not admissible except as provided by rule
or statute.” 9 But statements that are subject to a hearsay exception “are not excluded by the rule
against hearsay.” 10 Attachment RD-17 is subject to two of those exceptions: (1) the public-records
exception and (2) the statements-in-ancient-documents exception.

        1.        Attachment RD-17 is subject to the public-records hearsay exception.
       First, the public-records exception. Rule 803(8) of the Texas Rules of Evidence excludes
from the hearsay rule:

          A record or statement of a public office if: (A) it sets out: (i) the office’s activities;
         (ii) a matter observed while under a legal duty to report . . . ; or (iii) . . . factual
         findings from a legally authorized investigation; and (B) the opponent fails to
         demonstrate that the source of information or other circumstances indicate a lack
         of trustworthiness. 11

        Here, Attachment RD-17 is a record or statement of TPWD, 12 which is unquestionably a
public office or public agency. 13 And although Attachment RD-17 must “set[] out” only one of
Rule 803(8)’s three categories, 14 Attachment RD-17 fits within all three.
        Attachment RD-17 sets out TPWD’s activities and factual findings in response to the 62nd
Legislature charging TPWD with “conduct[ing] a study of Texas waterways.” 15 As TPWD ex-
plains, “[t]he information presented in th[e] [TPWD Report] was acquired as the result of on-site
inspections and an inventory taken in conjunction with this study.” 16 So Attachment RD-17 fits
within both the first (office activities) and third (factual findings from a legally authorized inves-
tigation) categories. Further, the 62nd Legislature required TPWD to conduct a study and report
on “the feasibility of a trail and waterway system in Texas.” 17 So Attachment RD-17 fits within
the second category (matters observed while under a legal duty to report) as well.
        Once a party demonstrates that a record or statement is within one of Rule 803(8)’s three
categories, then the record or statement is not excluded as hearsay unless the opponent of the record
or statement “demonstrate[d] that the source of information or other circumstances indicate a lack
of trustworthiness.” 18 Here, the Applicants (the opponent) failed to demonstrate—or even allege—

placed on the party opposing the admission of the report to show its untrustworthiness”).

 that the source of Attachment RD-17 (an official report of TPWD as archived on TPWD’s website)
or any other circumstances indicate a lack of trustworthiness. 19 And the Applicants cannot do so.
        The TPWD Report was drafted in response to a legislative charge over 50 years ago, so the
presumption of trustworthiness is strong. Governmental agencies, like TPWD, responding to leg-
islative mandates have every incentive to prepare accurate and reliable reports. 20 And TPWD ob-
viously had no adversarial stake in this proceeding when preparing a report over 50 years before
the Applicants initiated the proceeding.
        So Attachment RD-17, the TPWD Report, is properly subject to Rule 803(8)’s public-rec-
ords exception and should not be excluded by the rule against hearsay.

         2.         Attachment RD-17 is also subject to the statements-in-ancient-documents
                    hearsay exception.
       Second, the statements-in-ancient-documents exception. Rule 803(16) of the Texas Rules
of Evidence excludes from the hearsay rule “[a] statement in a document that is at least 20 years
old and whose authenticity is established.” 21
        Attachment RD-17 (the TPWD Report) satisfies the first prong: TPWD published the re-
port in September 1974—over 51 years ago. 22
        For the second prong (establishment of authenticity), the party offering the statement must
demonstrate that the document (1) is in such condition as to create no suspicion concerning its
authenticity and (2) was in a place where it would likely be found if it were authentic. 23
        Here, Attachment RD-17 is self-authenticating as “[a] book, pamphlet, or other publication
purporting to be issued by a public authority.” 24 Moreover, Mr. Davee found Attachment RD-17

to make false reports, and that public inspection of the reports will disclose inaccuracies.”); see also Tex. Pen. Code
§ 37.10(a)(1) (establishing as a Class A misdemeanor for the offense of “knowingly mak[ing] a false entry in, or false

 on the official TPWD website, 25 which is exactly where one would expect to find an authentic
TPWD report. And Attachment RD-17 (the web version of the TPWD Report) is identical to the
original, print version of the TPWD Report. 26 As an official report of TPWD issued in response to
a legislative charge, Attachment RD-17 does not raise any suspicions concerning its authenticity.
        Attachment RD-17 is over 20 years old with established authenticity. So it is properly sub-
ject to Rule 803(16)’s statements-in-ancient-documents exception and should not be excluded.

B.      Attachment RD-19 is not offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted in the Cush-
        way Study.
         Hearsay is “a statement that: (1) the declarant does not make while testifying at the current
trial or hearing; and (2) a party offers in evidence to prove the truth of the matter asserted in the
statement.” 27 “When a party offers a statement simply to show that it was made rather than to show
its truth or falsity, however, the hearsay rule does not bar its admission.”28 And “the hearsay rule
does not bar the admission of evidence for the purpose of establishing notice.” 29
         Attachment RD-19, the Cushway Study, asserts that (1) “pool dimensions, thermal condi-
tions, past dryness (number of years a pool was dry between 2004 and 2020), underlying geology,
and aquatic and riparian vegetation influence the abundance and species richness of freshwater
mussels in pools that may serve as important refuges for mussels to avoid desiccation and lethal
high temperatures” and (2) “pools that retain water during drought conditions (i.e., perennial pools)
may serve as ecological refuges for globally imperilled organisms such as freshwater mussels on
shorter timescales (e.g., days to years).” 30

          As interesting as those assertions may be, Mr. Davee isn’t offering Attachment RD-19 to
prove the truthfulness or accuracy of the Cushway Study’s assertions. Instead, Mr. Davee offers
Attachment RD-19 to show his knowledge that “scientific sampling . . . has been conducted in the
San Saba River and on [his] property, as well as other San Saba River segments above and below
the DTR Ranch.” 31
         Attachment RD-19 also supports his testimony that (1) he “allowed Kiara Cushway from
the Biology Department of Texas State University in San Marcos to access and study the DTR
Ranch and its San Saba River frontage to confirm the presence of mussel species in [his] section
of the San Saba River” 32 and (2) “Ms. Cushway accessed [his] property, took mussel samples from
the San Saba River along the DTR Ranch, and provided [him] with her observations through her
published report.” 33 And Attachment RD-19 shows that Mr. Davee had notice of “the presence of
the Texas Fatmucket [mussel] in the San Saba River at the proposed Link M33 crossing” 34 regard-
less of the truth or accuracy of the Cushway Study’s assertion on that matter.
         Attachment RD-19 is not offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted in the Cushway
Study. So Attachment RD-19 is not hearsay, and the Applicants’ objection should be overruled.

                                        II.      Non-Expert Opinion
       The Applicants incorrectly argue that Mr. Davee’s Attachments RD-17 and RD-19 “consti-
tute impermissible expert testimony by an unqualified witness.” 35 The Applicants’ boilerplate ob-
jection is that witnesses, including Mr. Davee, “are providing opinions concerning technical mat-
ters such as the potential health effects of electric and magnetic fields, wildlife biology, ecology,
hydrology, property valuation and appraisals, electric engineering, power flow dynamics, or legal
requirements.” 36 As to Attachments RD-17 and RD-19 specifically, the Applicants merely labeled
the attachments as “Non-Expert Opinion” without any further explanation or reasoning. 37
        But neither Attachment RD-17 nor Attachment RD-19 constitutes impermissible expert
testimony by an unqualified witness. Mr. Davee is not providing any expert opinions concerning
any technical matters contained in those attachments. (And Attachments RD-17 and RD-19 don’t
even address “potential health effects of electric and magnetic fields, . . . property valuation and

 appraisals, electric engineering, power flow dynamics, or legal requirements.” 38) Instead, Mr.
Davee is testifying to matters that he has personal knowledge of. 39 Importantly, the Applicants do
not object to any of Mr. Davee’s statements in his testimony.40
        Regarding Attachment RD-17, Mr. Davee simply testified about the existence of the TPWD
Report and that its description of the San Saba River matched his personal observations of the San
Saba River. 41 None of that is impermissible expert testimony by an unqualified witness—it’s all
within Mr. Davee’s personal knowledge. Mr. Davee did not attempt to rely on Attachment RD-17
as expert opinion or provide expert opinion about Attachment RD-17.
        And regarding Attachment RD-19, Mr. Davee testified only that Ms. Cushway requested
and was given access to his property, conducted a study on his property, and then sent him a copy
of her study (Attachment RD-19), which, in part, aligned with what Mr. Davee personally observed
on his land: the presence of Texas Fatmucket mussels in the San Saba River adjacent to his ranch.42
All of that is within Mr. Davee’s personal knowledge. Mr. Davee did not attempt to provide an
analysis of the Cushway Study’s data, draw scientific conclusions from the Cushway Study, or
substitute the Cushway Study for his own personal knowledge.
        Mr. Davee did not offer any expert opinions on technical matters in any of his testimony
regarding Attachments RD-17 and RD-19, and he did not include the TPWD Report or Cushway
Study to provide expert-opinion testimony. Because Mr. Davee did not provide any impermissible
expert testimony, the Applicants’ non-expert-opinion objection to Attachments RD-17 and RD-19
should be overruled.

                                                III.     Conclusion
        For these reasons, the M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners respectfully request
that the ALJs (1) overrule the Applicants’ objections to Attachments RD-17 and RD-19 and (2)
deny the Applicants’ motion to strike those two attachments.
